task: Hearth & Horizon story: galvanic corrosion from copper roof runoff (after a first story on frost heave was beaten to main by #16124)
errors: First frost model run used dz=0.02 m with dt=1800 s (explicit scheme unstable) and reported 0 m frost; caught and rerun at dz=0.025 m, dt=150 s with numpy.

Wrote a full frost-heave story ('A Metre Forty', ~5,200 words) from the bible's one open H&H proposal; at merge time PR #16124 had landed 'The Water That Walks Up' from the same proposal minutes earlier, near-identical in setting (near Sejny, 1931 bell, 78-year-old mason). Dropped it and wrote a second story from a proposal this run drafted itself.

doc_friction.issue: 'Pick the project that has gone longest without a new piece' via git log is unreliable on the shallow clone: the last 15 commits touching the folders all looked like hearth-and-horizon, while saints-by-candlelight episodes dated 2026-11-15 already existed. Episode front-matter dates were the better signal.

Finishing the only open Hearth & Horizon proposal leaves the shelf empty, so the run has to write a new proposal and probe overlap.mjs several times (water hammer, heat pump, borehole all taken) before finding an unused subject; a short list of unused subjects would save a run several minutes.

With one open proposal per shelf, two parallel creative runs both took the same proposal and produced near-identical stories; the open-PR search found nothing because the other run opened its PR late. A claim marker (e.g. an early draft PR or a 'claimed by <session>' line pushed first) or two proposals per shelf would cut collisions.
